_role: The ONE home of every weight the autonomy scorer applies. research/autonomy/priority.py types no weight; it reads them from here. Changing a research priority means editing this file, and the diff is the record of why the queue moved.
_objective: Advance EMC treatment. Every weight below is an answer to 'how much does this field move a patient closer', and nothing else.
_read_this_when: The queue's top item looks wrong. Do not special-case the item — fix the weight, and say in the commit message which reading of the objective changed.

live.reads: systems/graph/publications.json[].outcome_potential == 'live_positive', AND routes.json[].state.work_state != 'dead', AND closure_kind in (open, unset)
live.why: CLAUDE.md §0: pursue routes that could still produce a result. This is the largest single term on purpose.

patient_path.why: The north star is reaching a patient, and the program has no wet lab — so how the endpoint reaches one is the difference between a result and an activity.

pursue_now.why: A recorded judgement that waiting does not make this cheaper or better.

tier_one.why: The options memo's tier, used ONLY as a coarse prior. Its Axis D input is deliberately not read — see _forbidden_inputs.

endpoint_reachable.why: CLAUDE.md §5: every route's end goal is a paper. A route that can reach one today is nearer the only channel this program has.

blocker_leverage.reads: count of OTHER routes sharing at least one blocker with this route (capped by blocker_leverage_cap)
blocker_leverage.why: Retiring a widely-inherited blocker moves many routes at once. Per-route weight is small because the count does the work.

cost.reads: cost_class_rank: free=0, cheap=1, expensive=2 — derived from routes.json[].next.cost, never typed here
cost.why: CLAUDE.md §5: cost sequences and right-sizes work; it never skips a decision-relevant run. Hence a penalty small enough that an expensive live route still outranks a free dead one.

blocked_on_human.reads: routes.json[].state.authorization == 'needs_decision', or next.blocked_on naming a decision only trimcrae can make
blocked_on_human.why: The loop cannot advance it this cycle. Not -inf: it must stay visible enough to be escalated.

fruitless_attempts.why: A route that has swallowed attempts without producing evidence is telling you something. Decays its own priority instead of needing a human to notice.

patient_path_scale._why: Ordered by what this program can actually cause with no wet lab. 'named_bench' is an ASK of someone else and is discounted, not excluded — the options memo's Axis W1 is about whether that taker is self-interested, and that judgement is a human's.

cost_class_rank._why: CLAUDE.md §2's own ladder. A dollar figure is NEVER typed here or in priority.py — research/compute/pricing.md owns every cost, and an entry points at its rung.

negative_never_outranks_live.why: CLAUDE.md §0: a negative is a byproduct, never the objective. Weights alone will eventually let a well-graded finished write-up win — the highest-graded route in the portfolio today (RT-METHODS-PAPER, 'Tier 1, rank 1') is exactly that shape. This is a hard clamp applied AFTER scoring, not a weight.

blocked_without_evidence_becomes_a_check.why: CLAUDE.md §0: 'blocked' is a claim that needs evidence and it is usually wrong. Such an entry is not filtered out — it is re-emitted as a kind:'fetch' entry that re-tests the block, because most blocked rows wait on a $0 observation.

_forbidden_inputs.axis_d: What we would end up HOLDING if the experiment never happens. It structurally promotes finished work over live leads and is a human tiebreaker only — CLAUDE.md §0. priority.py must never read it, and test_the_scorer_never_reads_axis_d asserts so.
_forbidden_inputs.aixiv_rating: Unauthenticated and trivially forgeable — .claude/skills/aixiv-submission/SKILL.md §0. Never an input to anything.
_forbidden_inputs.recency: How recently a route was touched is not evidence about whether it can produce a result.
